root_cause.text: The debugfs entry for "trace_mask" was passing an incorrect private data pointer (`fw_trace` instead of `pvr_dev`) to the file operations handler, causing `pvr_fw_trace_mask_set()` to dereference a NULL or invalid pointer when accessing the device structure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes line 561 from `debugfs_create_file("trace_mask", 0600, dir, fw_trace, &pvr_fw_trace_mask_fops)` to `debugfs_create_file("trace_mask", 0600, dir, pvr_dev, &pvr_fw_trace_mask_fops)`. The `pvr_fw_trace_mask_fops` file operations expect `pvr_dev` as the private data context, but the buggy code was passing `fw_trace` instead. This mismatch caused the handler function `pvr_fw_trace_mask_set()` to receive and attempt to cast/dereference an incorrect data pointer, resulting in the NULL pointer dereference at address 0x0 shown in the crash trace. The bug was introduced in commit a331631496a0 which simplified module parameters but failed to update this debugfs registration call accordingly.

intent_record.what: Changed the fourth argument to debugfs_create_file() from 'fw_trace' to 'pvr_dev' on line 561.
intent_record.how: This changes which data structure is passed as the private data pointer to the debugfs file operations. The file operations handler (&pvr_fw_trace_mask_fops) will now receive 'pvr_dev' instead of 'fw_trace' when accessed, allowing the handler to access device-level context rather than trace-specific context.

Author: Matt Coster <matt.coster@imgtec.com>

    drm/imagination: Simplify module parameters
    
    We had a whole load of bloaty infrastructure to deal with module parameters
    in a way that's wholly unnecessary. Strip it all back to basics to make
    adding new parameters less of a headache.
    
    Reviewed-by: Alessio Belle <alessio.belle@imgtec.com>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260113-devic
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the debugfs_create_file() call at lines 501-502. The function passes `fw_trace` as the private data pointer (4th argument) to debugfs_create_file(), but the file operations handlers `pvr_fw_trace_mask_get()` and `pvr_fw_trace_mask_set()` (lines 463-477) expect to receive `pvr_dev` as the data parameter. Both functions cast the data pointer to `struct pvr_device *pvr_dev` and dereference it (lines 466 and 471). Since `fw_trace` is passed instead of `pvr_dev`, the handlers will dereference an incorrect pointer, causing a NULL or invalid pointer dereference. The fix would require passing `pvr_dev` instead of `fw_trace` to debugfs_create_file().
